What would happen if you were to take a vehicle engine up to a hundred thousand RPM and how would you go about doing so?
I'd use a turbine. Dump a shitload of fuel in it. And run far far away.

The first question we need to ask is what kind of engine and how you define the term motor. There are many electric motors with 100,000 RPMs at the shaft. Combustion engines wouldn't be able to withstand the heat. I sort of recall a jet engine spinning up to 80k, but that memory is fuzzy and Google is too far away.

If it's your standard vehicle Otto cycle engine the main issues are going to be heat buildup, valve train bounce and extreme stress on the crank main bearing caps, crank, rods, pistons and rings. I can't see a steel timing chain surviving either so there goes the cam too. Oil delivery would probably also be an issue.

Another problem - if you can get it to reliably inject - is that the fuel flame front in the cylinder would never get the chance to propagate because of the high crank speed. This in itself would be a nightmare to solve.

If somehow you got to 100k rpm, breakages aside, nothing would happen although the torque figure would be interesting.

It would be hard to avoid throwing a rod or something similarly catastrophic. Also, at that speed, valve springs would be completely unable to close the valves fully, so something like Ducati's desmodromic cam type system would be required, to open and close valves without the relatively slow spring assistance.

I also wonder just how efficient air/fuel combustion could possibly be in such a miniscule amount of time given to compression and ignition due to the insanely high rpm cycle. I expect F1 engineers have resolved much of this in ways with which I am unfamiliar, but still, 100k RPM is really nutty. If this kind of rotational velocity is required, a gas turbine would most likely be more sensible.
